t: This is the Old Burial Ground of the Royal Hospital Chelsea, a cemetery for people associated with the hospital. It sits at the north east corner of the grounds, alongside the London Road. Buried here is General Sir Neville Lyttelton, who lived from 1845 to 1931. He was a British Army officer who served against the Fenian Raids and in the Anglo-Egyptian War, the Mahdist War and the Second Boer War. He later became Chief of the General Staff and then Commander-in-Chief, Ireland.
